game: Kent State Golden Flashes@Ohio State Buckeyes

guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our slight lean toward Ohio State starts with its ability to create scoring opportunities against a Kent State defense that has struggled to prevent them. Our numbers see a major advantage there, and the supporting context is strong: Ohio State produced 671 yards in its opener, returns eight offensive starters and brought back 85.8 percent of its 2025 offensive-line snaps. We are not treating one result as proof, but the continuity helps explain why our model expects Ohio State to sustain drives and generate repeated scoring chances.

The other side of the matchup points in the same direction. Kent State grades poorly in both rushing efficiency and scoring-opportunity creation, while Ohio State rates near the top of our defensive measures in those areas. Our concern is that Ohio State replaced eight defensive starters, so we do not want to overstate the certainty of those ratings this early. The market is already pricing an extremely one-sided game, and our disagreement is too small to create enough value for us.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
For us, the matchup to watch is Kent State's rushing offense against Ohio State's run defense. If Kent State cannot create efficient early-down runs, its path to sustained possessions becomes narrow, which matters when Ohio State's offense is positioned to generate frequent scoring opportunities.

We saw Ohio State hold Ball State to 45 rushing yards in the opener. That does not automatically settle the question against a different opponent, especially with the defensive turnover, but it supports the underlying mismatch our numbers identify.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 home win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Against Ball State, Ohio State produced 671 total yards: 434 passing and 237 rushing.
Ohio State held Ball State to 165 total yards, including 45 rushing and 120 passing.
Fourteen Ohio State players recorded a reception against Ball State, the program's first game with at least 14 receivers making a catch since Sept. 22, 2018 against Tulane.

opponent_notes.fact: Ohio State is scheduled to host Kent State at noon on Sept. 19, 2026, with FOX carrying the game.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin is a returning offensive starter and entered 2026 with 15 starts in 19 career games.
Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes in 2025, led the nation in completion percentage, and threw for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns with eight interceptions.
Sayin entered the Texas game with a 76.4 percent career completion rate and seven career 300-yard passing games.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned eight offensive starters for 2026: QB Julian Sayin, RB Bo Jackson, WR Jeremiah Smith, WR Brandon Inniss, OT Phillip Daniels, C Carson Hinzman, OG Luke Montgomery and OG Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half against Ball State.
Bo Jackson rushed for 1,090 yards on 179 carries in 2025 and averaged 9.2 yards per carry in the 2026 opener, including a career-long 65-yard touchdown.
Transfer wide receiver Devin McCuin arrived from UTSA after recording 65 receptions for 726 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025.
Transfer wide receiver Kyle Parker arrived from LSU with 34 career receptions for 385 yards and five touchdowns.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned three defensive starters for 2026: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters from 2025: defensive tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, defensive end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.
Ohio State added defensive tackle James Smith and defensive end Qua Russaw as transfers from Alabama.
Ohio State added linebacker Christian Alliegro from Wisconsin; he entered 2026 with 127 career tackles and eight sacks.
Ohio State added safety Earl Little Jr. from Florida State after he led FSU with 76 tackles in 2025.
Ohio State added defensive tackle John Walker from UCF; he entered 2026 with 64 career tackles, eight tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen is Ohio State's run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

offensive_context.fact: Ohio State entered its second game ranked third nationally in total offense and passing offense after producing 56 points and 671 yards in the opener.
Ohio State converted five of 11 third downs in the opener and scored on every red-zone possession.
Ohio State returned 85.8 percent of its 2025 offensive-line snaps among players who logged at least 100 snaps, the highest listed continuity rate among Power Four teams.
After the opener, Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts.
The returning offensive linemen include Carson Hinzman with 36 career starts, Austin Siereveld with 21, Phillip Daniels with 17 and Luke Montgomery with 17.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in its season opener against Ball State.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed three points, 165 total yards and no red-zone score in its season-opening win over Ball State.
Ball State converted 21.4 percent of its third downs against Ohio State.
Ohio State's 2025 defense led the FBS in scoring defense at 9.3 points allowed per game, total defense at 219.1 yards per game and passing defense at 129.7 yards per game.
Since the start of the 2024 season, Ohio State had allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games and had nine games without allowing a touchdown.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's only returning specialist starter.
Ohio State lost starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann after the 2025 season.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State entered the Texas game 1-0 and ranked No. 1 in the Associated Press poll.
Ohio State had 34 returning letterwinners and 31 letterwinners lost entering the 2026 season.
